request.spec:
Show a rate calendar: for each grade and each month of the sheet's today's calendar year, the
rate in force on the first day of that month (n/a when none).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Show a rate calendar: for each grade and each month of the sheet's today's calendar year, the
rate in force on the first day of that month (n/a when none).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
I added the rate calendar, and all 4 acceptance tests in `bin/e2e` now pass.

It's a new table on the main screen, just below the existing Rates section. It has one row for each grade (A, B, C) and one column for each month of the sheet's today's calendar year. Each cell shows the rate in force on the 1st of that month, or `n/a` when there isn't one.

The change is front-end only: one new file, `src/main/frontend/features/rates/calendar.slot.tsx`. Each cell reuses the existing `rateOf` lookup that already fills the "Rate % today" column. So the calendar follows the same rules as that column: a rate's end date is respected, a later-starting rate takes over, and a parent sheet's rates are used when the sheet has none. No server, stored-data or audit changes were needed.
